Generally we would spell these out, unless these are register names, not addresses themselves?

This is how the spec defines these fields.
ERR<n>FR 8 8 Contents of the Error Record Feature Register.
ERR<n>CTLR 8 16 Contents of the Error Record Control Register
ERR<n>STATUS 8 24 Contents of the Error Record Primary Status Register.
ERR<n>ADDR 8 32 Contents of the Error Record Address Register.
ERR<n>MISC0 8 40 Contents of the Error Record Miscellaneous Register 0.
ERR<n>MISC1 8 48 Contents of the Error Record Miscellaneous Register 1.
ERR<n>MISC2 8 56 Content of the Error Record Miscellaneous Register 2.
ERR<n>MISC3 8 64 Content of the Error Record Miscellaneous Register 3.

So then these would be:
errorRecordFeatureRegister: 1
errorRecordControlRegister: 1

ect

This is a great comment!
We're safe because of the RAS System Arch (as defined in Arm IHI0100)>

Header size is 80 bytes.
each entry of the error_syndrome_array is 72 bytes.
There are at most 896 entries in the error_syndrome_array (if FEAT_RASSA_64KB_GRP is implemented, more details are in the Arm IHI0100).

So, architecturally, the maximum value of node.AuxiliaryDataOffset=80 + 896*72 = 64592 < 2^16.

Looks like the select_section_by_guid fuzz hook exists because everything downstream hangs off that GUID dispatch. Without a fuzz‑only override, most of the code in sections would be effectively unreachable from a fuzzer.
